title: Trace Stream Gateway: Kafka proxy with schema negotiation and tenant hinting
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a lightweight Trace Stream Gateway (TSG) that sits between Redwoods OTLP/Jaeger ingesters and downstream Kafka-based tracing backends. The gateway performs schema negotiation, per-tenant header hinting, adaptive batching, and upstream-friendly backpressure signaling. This ticket implements the core proxy, schema version detection, and a tenant-hinting header strategy needed for partner onramps that cannot speak native OTLP directly.
acceptance_criteria: Gateway accepts OTLP/gRPC and Jaeger thrift/http spans and emits compressed Avro or Protobuf messages to Kafka topics per tenant
Per-tenant schema version selection works via a header (X-Redwood-Tenant-Version) or via tenant profile lookup in Redis; oldest schema fallback path validated
Backpressure: when Kafka producer latency or queue depth exceeds thresholds, gateway returns HTTP 429 or gRPC RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED and exposes metrics for shed/queue-size
End-to-end test harness validates no-span-loss for 99% of 1k rps synthetic trace workload under normal conditions and graceful degradation under overload
Integration documented in Console onboarding guide and example kinesis/kafka consumer mapping provided
design_notes: Proxy runs as a stateless sidecar or autoscaled Deployment; uses a small local ring buffer for transient batching
Schema negotiation: support three canonical encodings (avro-v1, avro-v2, proto-v1); include schema-id in Kafka message header for consumer compatibility
Tenant hinting order: X-Redwood-Tenant -> Authorization bearer token mapping -> tenant-lookup fallback via tenant-map service
Backpressure mechanics: expose internal producer lag metric and if lag > 500ms for > 5s, flip to shed mode and surface metric 'tsg.shed_mode_active'
Security: use mTLS for upstream and SASL/SSL for Kafka; redact PII fields according to tenant policy during transform
rollout_plan: Canary deploy to trace-ingest namespace with 5 pods and 10% traffic routing via traffic-split flag
Observe 'export-latency' and 'producer-queue-depth' for 48 hours before ramping to 50%
If shed_rate > 0.5% for 2 continuous hours, rollback to previous configuration
Provide a console toggle to enable per-tenant schema negotiation for early-adopter customers
test_plan: Unit tests for schema-selector and header-parsing logic (edge cases: missing header, malformed schema-id)
Integration tests with local Kafka cluster using docker-compose and three consumer versions to validate compatibility
Load test: 5k rps short soak and 1k rps 1-hour soak with synthetic KV cache warm-up
Chaos test: kill 30% of gateway pods and assert no data loss in prioritized tenant topic within 30s recovery window
risks: Schema evolution mismatches could lead to consumer deserialization errors - mitigation: schema-id header and consumer-side tolerant parsing
Backpressure signaling may cause caller retries to amplify load - mitigation: document retry-after and implement token-bucket client guidance
Increased operational cost for stateful buffering if mis-configured - mitigation: enforce bounded buffer sizes and autoscale policies
